criteria.name: Correct identity and source-backed footprint
criteria.evidence: Purdue GIS FID 791 and Acacia's official contact/history pages identify the 608 Waldron Street house. The WGS84 and EPSG:2968 rings agree within 0.226 m² (0.049%). The modeled structural shell overlaps the GIS ring at IoU 0.933; it is smaller by -0.609%, with 3.211 m maximum boundary residual. The GIS ring includes a small southern projection consistent with the modeled entrance/porch; the shell itself remains unshifted.
findings: The ArcGIS Shape__Area/Shape__Length summary fields conflict materially with the encoded polygon. The encoded rings are mutually consistent and were used, but the structural shell does not reproduce the entire southern projection.

criteria.name: Position, orientation, and scale/dimensions
criteria.evidence: Fresh-open inspection confirms the original direct campus-coordinate frame, zero object/collection offset, and main-shell bounds [[-334.7135, -315.2749], [342.1364, 370.6293], [0.0, 9.45]] m. The north-up Esri overlay shows the FID 791 footprint aligned with the roof and west-side approach path. Matching that path to the official porch elevation supports the front-bearing inference.
findings: The official facade photo is not geotagged and the Esri tile acquisition date is undisclosed, so the west-facing bearing is an inference rather than surveyed or direct photo orientation.

criteria.name: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
criteria.evidence: Official renovation/elevation drawings show three above-grade floor levels and a basement; the modeled envelope reaches 9.45 m above the asset datum. The saved facade photo and plans support a dark shingle pitched roof, central front gable, dormers, and chimney, which are represented in the asset.
findings: The plan set may depict renovation/project design rather than the fully verified as-built condition. Floor spacing, overall roof height, and roof geometry remain estimated.

criteria.name: Facade, entrances, and distinctive architecture
criteria.evidence: Direct comparison of the saved chapter facade photo and model render shows the distinctive brick tower and vertical ACACIA lettering, central illuminated-name entry arch, pale porch frame, brick lower facade, cream infill with dark timber framing above, central gable, repeated windows, dormers, and chimney. The render now places the half-timber gable above the entrance. The modeled interior depicts plan-supported lobby/atrium, heritage room, study hall, bedrooms, stairs, and circulation; the room plan is schematic.
findings: The entry arch lettering and illumination have low contrast in the render, and facade/window/porch proportions remain simplified compared with the photograph and architectural elevations.
The interior is legible as a schematic cutaway but uses estimated room placement, furnishings, and finishes; it is not verified as-built.

criteria.name: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
criteria.evidence: Fresh-open asset has the expected stable scene/collection, 508 objects and 502 meshes; 13 local materials; 0 meshes missing material slots; 0 unpacked absolute image paths; and 0 linked Blend libraries. The source folder preserves GIS, official plans, facade imagery, aerial overlay, provenance, validation, and exterior/interior renders.
